condensed:
The devin-orchestrator is a ~1200-line, deterministic, gh-CLI-driven Python pipeline (no LangGraph, no agent SDK) that turns GitHub issues labeled `automated-ready` into merged PRs, using AI coding agents (Devin CLI, or Claude Code in worktrees) as disposable workers and a second AI pass as adversarial reviewer. It existed as untracked, duplicated code in job-cannon and empericus, drifting independently — the new standalone repo (already scaffolded at devin-orchestrator, 41 tests green, union merge done for merge/label decoupling, config discovery, prompt-dir overrides, worker_template selection) is the fix for that duplication.

Flow: intake (snapshot ready-labeled issues) → dispatch (pick dispatchable issues, render worker prompt, hand to an adapter — manual manifest or command subprocess) → worker executes out-of-process (git worktree per issue off origin/main, junctioned shared venv, headless CLI launch, self-serves test/commit/push/PR via gh) → review (snapshot PR/checks/diff, render adversarial packet, optional cross-family second-model pass) → record-review (human/AI records approved/request_changes/blocked) → merge-ready (gates on approved decision + green required checks, squash-merges, labels done) → loop (chains all of the above, designed for repeated invocation with GitHub labels + on-disk artifacts as the only durable state).

8 of 13 modules are byte-identical across forks; workflow.py/config.py/github.py/__main__.py/orchestrator.config.yaml/worker.md diverge. job-cannon uniquely has cross-family adversarial review + spec-review; empericus uniquely has `dispatch --issues` explicit wave dispatch and a merge_pr empty-stdout fix job-cannon lacks. state.json (version 1, issues/prs/events) is a lossy cache — production evidence shows review()/intake() wholesale-clobber state entries, dropping recorded decisions; on-disk artifacts (review-decision.json) are the real authority.

Devin CLI has no session-creation/lifecycle API (confirmed empirically); only shell-wrapping works. Design docs reach contradictory verdicts same-day (fallback-analysis.md: stay manual; realistic-path-forward.md: build devin-shell with care) — the fleet operationally converged on the latter via setup_worker.sh/finish_worker.sh: per-issue git worktree off origin/main, junctioned shared venv (critical Windows hazard: worktree removal follows the junction and deletes the shared venv unless the reparse point is deleted first), headless `devin --prompt-file --print --permission-mode dangerous` launched backgrounded so exit re-wakes the orchestrating session. Output capture is the weakest link: --print only emits a final message at exit, producing 0-byte logs on interruption and 39-byte "tool rejected" deaths (8+ observed) even under dangerous mode. Claude Code workers in empericus are an emergent pattern with zero bespoke code: git worktree + inherited tracked .claude/settings.json hooks + human pasting worker-prompt.md — and in practice humans merge PRs directly, bypassing merge-ready entirely, leaving issue labels stalled at agent:in-progress.

The dossier's §7 delivers a prioritized, deduplicated bug list (34 items, P0-P3): highest-confidence P0s are the merge_pr stdout/stderr bug (emp fixed, jc didn't), shell injection via issue-title interpolation in string-form dispatch_command, the manual adapter's fabricated-success contract, state.json clobbering that drops recorded review decisions, no state locking, cross-family failure stubs being reused as permanent success, inconsistent Windows subprocess encoding, and the shared-venv-junction-deletion hazard enforced only by a shell comment. P2/P3 items target exactly what the scaffold still needs: devin-shell adapter build items (fix the design docs' own internal contradictions — undocumented --permission-mode bypass value, missing --print in the reference implementation, unresolved whether --print sessions even persist to sessions.db, a session-attribution SQLite race), a Claude Code adapter that codifies the emergent worktree pattern into real code plus a reconciliation pass for human-merged PRs, and a doctor command cross-checking required_checks against live gh output.

External research (§10) contributes concrete, HIGH-applicability additions folded into the fix list: a deterministic pre-review "janitor" gate (verify CI is terminal, diff non-empty, PR description non-empty — before spending any LLM review call); re-scoping the adversarial review prompt to target undocumented architectural intent rather than re-deriving correctness CI already checked (backed by a controlled study showing correlated AI-reviewer blind spots with AI generators); treating cross-model review as an independent veto channel never a consensus vote; a hard rework-cycle cap (1-2) with escalation to human rather than indefinite retry (backed by empirical interaction-round CDFs and a documented "agentic ghosting" pattern on vague feedback); deterministic pre-filters (file-count/diff-size/empty-description) before any LLM review spend; and an intake-time admission checklist (stated success criteria + verification command + bounded scope) gating the automated-ready label itself, backed by an AUC-0.96 predictor of high-review-effort PRs from static features alone.

The dossier closes with 14 open design questions requiring panel input, most critically: which devin-shell strategy doc is canonical, whether --print sessions persist to sessions.db at all (load-bearing for the SQLite-tracking design), where review decisions should durably live given the "GitHub is authoritative" promise is currently false, whether .devin/ hooks+skills infra is in scope, and how aggressively rework cycles should cap/escalate.
fix_list: P0: Adopt empericus's merge_pr fix (return `output or f"merged #{number}"` on empty stdout) since gh pr merge prints success to stderr; add a test pinning merged=True on empty stdout (currently masked by both forks' FakeGitHub test doubles).

P0: Remove/harden shell=True string-form dispatch_command — issue_title is .format-interpolated directly into a shell string (shell injection via attacker-controlled issue titles); require list-form only or pass values via env/argv.

P0: Make the manual adapter's ok=True honest — it currently reports success with zero session launched, causing agent:in-progress to be applied before any worker exists; ok should mean 'manifest written, awaiting confirmation.'

P0: Fix state.json clobbering — review() and intake() wholesale-overwrite state['prs'][n]/state['issues'][n], erasing recorded decisions and dispatch status (confirmed in production, pr-497 case); merge-update instead of dict-replace, or make on-disk review-decision.json the sole authority.
P0: Add state.json locking/safe read-modify-write and catch JSONDecodeError in load_state (currently an uncaught crash on corrupt/truncated state).

P0: Fix cross-family failure-stub reuse — a timeout/error stub satisfies the 'reuse if exists+non-empty' check and is treated as permanent success on every subsequent loop pass; mark stubs distinguishably and retry.

P0: Centralize subprocess execution in one runner with consistent encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', and bytes-safe TimeoutExpired handling — adapters.py currently lacks this (Windows cp1252 decode risk, uncaught UnicodeDecodeError, 'b\'...\' ' garbage in results).

P0: Port the shared-venv junction-deletion-safety ordering (delete the .venv reparse point via PowerShell .Delete() before git worktree remove --force) from the untracked finish_worker.sh into real, tested orchestrator code — currently a data-loss hazard protected only by a shell comment.
P1: Add per-PR error isolation in loop() — a single merge conflict currently aborts review/merge of every remaining PR in the batch via an uncaught GitHubError.

P1: Fix `dispatch --issues` parsing (empericus) — global space-deletion silently mismerges numbers ('5 6' -> 56), non-numeric tokens crash uncaught, duplicates aren't deduped, and --issues isn't plumbed through loop().
P1: Fix delete_branch default/YAML contradiction (empericus) — dataclass default True contradicts shipped YAML false; default to worktree-safe False or decouple merge from branch cleanup.
P1: Fix asymmetric/accumulating label transitions — unify into one transition function; wire or remove the vestigial agent:queued label; stop review()/loop() from stomping needs-rework on every pass.

P1: Enforce max_rework_cycles as a hard counter with auto-escalation to blocked/human-needed (currently dead config allowing indefinite rework loops) — cap at 1-2 cycles per external research on agent 'ghosting' on vague feedback.
P1: Tighten linked_issue_number — stop matching any bare '#N' in a PR title before checking qualified body keywords; mis-linking drives wrong labels/review/merge actions.
P1: Unify review-decision.json schema (record_review currently drops the required_changes field) and require a non-empty summary on record-review.
P1: Document/fix the SKIPPED-as-failed and duplicate-check-name-collapse behavior in summarize_checks.

P1: Replace the hardcoded readonly-command allowlist (_is_mutating) with an explicit per-method mutating flag; extend --dry-run coverage beyond gh calls to state writes and adapter/model subprocesses, or narrow the documented claim.

P1: Fence/escape injected prompt values (issue bodies, PR text) to close the prompt-injection channel via broken code fences; treat all worker-authored/issue-authored text as untrusted input to any LLM reviewer prompt.

P1: Fix empericus's rework.md referencing a dropped /preflight skill (byte-identical leftover from the job-cannon port) — generate worker and rework prompts from one shared per-fleet tooling profile so they cannot drift apart.
P1: Add a validation layer for config parsing with actionable section/key error messages instead of bare dataclass TypeErrors.

P2 (adapters): Build the devin-shell adapter per realistic-path-forward.md but fix its own contradictions first — use `--permission-mode dangerous` (not the undocumented 'bypass'), ensure `--print` is actually included in the launch call, and empirically resolve whether --print sessions persist to sessions.db before committing to SQLite-based session tracking.

P2 (adapters): Fix the session-attribution race in SQLite session-id polling (snapshot existing IDs/created_at before dispatch; consider `devin list --format json` instead of raw undocumented-schema reads).

P2 (adapters): Implement real output capture — wire --export per-turn transcript export and/or harvest %APPDATA%\devin\cli\transcripts\<id>.json post-exit; record structured exit code + timestamps per run.

P2 (adapters): Detect and auto-handle the 'Error: A tool was rejected by the user' 39-byte signature — classify as permission-abort, check for salvageable worktree progress, auto-relaunch with a finish-style prompt.
P2 (adapters): Add worker liveness/timeout supervision (track PID+start time; distinguish in-flight vs dead 0-byte logs; enforce max session duration with kill+salvage-relaunch).

P2 (Claude Code adapter): Codify the emergent worktree+inherited-.claude/-hooks pattern into real adapter code (automate worktree creation + headless prompt hand-off) instead of relying on manual assembly; add a reconciliation pass that detects PRs merged outside merge_ready() and corrects stale issue labels — the exact gap observed in empericus's live usage.
P2: Replace grep-based branch-name recovery from rendered prompt files with structured sidecar data.

P3: Add a `doctor` command cross-checking configured required_checks against live `gh pr checks --json name` output on a recent PR, surfacing mismatches as a detectable error instead of a silent permanent merge-block.

P3: Port the FLEET-READINESS-DESIGN.md hardening pattern (git-ls-remote PR-existence fallback for gh flakiness, bounded/budgeted diagnostic sub-probes on gate failures, diff-scoped fast contract-test gate before merge) into the new repo's gate layer, generalized via config-driven path-to-test mapping rather than hardcoded examples.
P3: Fix naive substring-based destructive-command blocking (would false-positive on legitimate `ruff format`) with word-boundary/argv-aware matching.
P3: Version the gate/hook layer in-repo with its own CI (ruff/format checks, embedded-script-literal hygiene scan, smoke tests) instead of leaving it as untracked WIP.

Testing: Promote FakeGitHub to one shared fixture with a typing.Protocol surface (fixes the observed drift where pr_checks canned names diverged between forks); add the missing merge_pr-empty-stdout test; fill coverage gaps (status/intake/bootstrap_labels/full record_review routing/loop end-to-end/dry-run gating/append_event cap).

Docs: Rebuild the 5-doc suite (README/ARCHITECTURE/QUICKSTART/RUNBOOK/WORKFLOWS) repo-agnostic with template variables for session name/repo root/required checks; document cross-family review, dispatch --issues, the command adapter, and exit codes, none of which appear anywhere in the current docs; add a dedicated worktree-fleet-model doc covering the junction hazard and backgrounded-launch pattern; migrate the unversioned .var design-doc corpus (FLEET-READINESS-DESIGN.md, devin-cli-reference.md, etc.) to a versioned docs location before it is lost.

External-research HIGH item: add a deterministic pre-review 'janitor' gate (CI terminal, diff non-empty, PR description non-empty, required-check names actually present) that runs before generating a review packet at all, catching the observed production pattern of empty-summary approvals and approvals granted while CI was still IN_PROGRESS.

External-research HIGH item: re-scope adversarial review prompts to target undocumented architectural/convention intent rather than re-deriving correctness that CI already checks (backed by a controlled study showing correlated AI-reviewer/AI-generator blind spots on domain-convention violations).

External-research HIGH item: add an intake-time admission checklist (stated success criteria, identifiable verification command, bounded scope) gating the automated-ready label itself, rather than accepting any labeled issue as dispatchable — backed by an AUC-0.96 predictor of high-review-effort PRs from static pre-dispatch features.
open_questions: Which devin-shell strategy doc is canonical — fallback-analysis.md ('stay manual, shell-wrapping fails all production requirements') or realistic-path-forward.md ('build devin-shell with care'), both dated the same day with opposite recommendations and no recorded supersession decision?

Does `devin --print` actually create a persistent row in sessions.db / a transcript file, or is it truly transient with no persistence? The design corpus contradicts itself on this and it is load-bearing for whether SQLite-based session tracking is viable at all for the devin-shell adapter.

What specifically triggers the 'Error: A tool was rejected by the user' 39-byte failure under --permission-mode dangerous — an org-enforced deny, a .devin/ hook veto, or a CLI bug in non-interactive permission handling?

Where should review decisions durably live, given the stated 'GitHub is authoritative, .var is regenerable' design promise is currently false for decisions (they exist only in local review-decision.json files)? Local-only-but-fixed, PR comment, PR label, or a real GitHub PR review?

Is the .devin/ hooks+skills infrastructure (push gates, 8 skills, 4 lifecycle hooks) in scope for this extraction as a shipped default, or does it remain host-repo-specific WIP that consuming repos bring themselves?
Should the new repo own worktree lifecycle (creation, naming, post-merge pruning) as first-class code, or remain operator-managed as empericus's delete_branch comment currently prescribes?

What is the intended default dispatch ordering — keep newest-first (today's implicit behavior) or build first-class dependency-ordered dispatch (e.g., parsing 'Depends on #N' from issue bodies), given empericus's real operational need for wave-ordered dispatch surfaced within hours of first live use?

What is the cross-family reviewer's runner when the Devin CLI isn't present at all in a pure-Claude-Code deployment — and should cross-family/spec-review become risk-scored per-PR rather than a single repo-wide enabled/disabled toggle?

Should worker prompts carry host-repo invariants via a per-repo template-override directory, or by instructing workers to read the host CLAUDE.md only — this is the concrete decision behind adopting a structured Devin-Playbook-style prompt template?

What should trigger the diff-scoped contract-test gate in the new repo (§7/P3 fleet-readiness item) — job-cannon's example is domain-specific; the new repo needs a config-driven path-to-test-subset mapping mechanism whose exact shape (globs, labels, diff content) is undecided.

Does the new repo need explicit per-worker-type routing/retry logic (retry a failed dispatch with a different worker architecture rather than the same one), or is that premature before enough dispatch history exists to know each worker type's actual failure fingerprint in this system?

How aggressively should max_rework_cycles escalate — a hard cap of 1 structured retry (matching cited production multi-agent-SWE practice) or 2-3 (matching the dead config value both forks already shipped but never enforced)?

Is the proposed janitor-style pre-review deterministic gate additive to the existing review pipeline (skip packet generation entirely on failure) or should it still generate the packet but pre-annotate it with findings for the human/reviewer to see?

What is the supported Python/OS floor for the standalone repo — is Linux/Mac a first-class target, or is this explicitly a Windows-first, single-operator tool given the extensive Windows-specific hazards (venv junctions, cp1252, PowerShell wrapper scripts) baked into current operational practice?

design.summary: The scaffold at /path/to/devin-orchestrator is materially further along than the dossier's status note claims: it already ships doctor.py (workflow-derived CI-check verification, item 31 DONE), cross_family.py + spec-review (jc's adversarial pass, ported), --issues wave dispatch (emp's fix, ported with proper strip/dedup — item 10 DONE), the merge_pr empty-stdout fix (item 1 DONE, verbatim emp fix with explanatory comment), and full merge/branch-deletion decoupling (item 11 DONE — delete_branch defaults False... actually defaults True in scaffold, see fixes list). 50/50 tests green (grew from the dossier's 41). This design covers everything genuinely remaining: the devin-shell and Claude-Code-worktree adapters, the janitor pre-review gate, rework-cycle enforcement, worktree-lifecycle safety, remaining P0/P1 correctness bugs not yet closed (shell-injection removal, subprocess encoding, state-clobbering in review()/intake(), locking/corrupt-state handling, label-transition centralization), doctor extensions, docs, and the two-repo migration to editable path deps with zero disruption to job-cannon's live 38.7KB/55-issue/7-PR/40-event state.json (verified in place, not the dossier's stated "4 in flight" — treat the real number as the constraint). Verified empericus has NO .var/devin-orchestrator state to migrate (nothing at risk there) and .devin/ hook/skill infra is job-cannon-only, confirming open question 5's resolution: ship it as an optional bring-your-own layer, not a package default.

design.adapter_design:
**Adapter Protocol** (`adapters/__init__.py`):
```python
class WorkerAdapter(Protocol):
    name: ClassVar[str]
    def dispatch(self, repo_root: Path, request: SessionRequest, config: OrchestratorConfig) -> SessionDispatchResult: ...
    def reconcile(self, repo_root: Path, state: dict) -> list[ReconciliationFinding]: ...  # default no-op for manual/command
```
`dispatch_sessions()` keeps its existing contract verbatim (manifest-first, always-write-results, item 3's "ok means manifest written" framing applied to `manual.py` only) and becomes a thin registry lookup (`{"manual": ManualAdapter(), "command": CommandAdapter(), "devin-shell": DevinShellAdapter(), "claude-code": ClaudeCodeAdapter()}`) instead of the current if/elif chain — this is the one place a "hardcoded list" is legitimate (it's an adapter registry, not domain data, and adding a 5th adapter is a one-line registration, exactly analogous to `argparse` subcommand registration).

**Which adapters ship, and why:**
1. **`manual`** (existing, fixed) — kept verbatim except honesty fix: `ok=True` now means "manifest written, awaiting operator confirmation" per item 3; `dispatch()` in workflow.py stops labeling `agent:in-progress` on manual-adapter success alone — instead `intake`'s next pass or an explicit `devin-orch confirm-dispatch --issue N` (new, tiny) flips the label once a human confirms a session actually started. This directly fixes the observed job-cannon divergence (manifest frozen at one issue while ~60 issue dirs existed) without removing the fallback's simplicity.
2. **`command`** (existing, fixed) — shell=True string-templating form REMOVED entirely (item 2, the shell-injection fix); only the list-form (`.format` per-argv-part, no shell) survives. This is a breaking config change for any consumer using string-form `dispatch_command` — none currently do in production (dossier confirms `command` adapter is "configured-but-unused in production in both forks"), so it's safe to remove rather than deprecate.
3. **`devin-shell`** (NEW, default-documented per user's DEFAULT requirement) — implements dossier items 22-28: `devin --prompt-file <FILE> --print --permission-mode dangerous --model <MODEL>` (validated flags, no `bypass`), subprocess via `subprocess_runner.py` (consistent encoding), PID+start-time tracked in a sidecar `session-<issue>.json` (not SQLite — resolves open question 2 by NOT depending on the contested premise; process exit code + `--export <path>` transcript + stdout capture is the tracking mechanism, sessions.db is never touched). `--export` captures the per-turn transcript to `.var/devin-orchestrator/logs/issue-<N>/export.json` for future doom-loop detection (dossier item I, explicitly deferred but the capture point ships now so it's not re-architected later). Classifies the 39-byte `"Error: A tool was rejected by the user"` stdout signature as `tool_rejected` (item 26) and returns `ok=False, error="tool_rejected"` — auto-relaunch is NOT automatic (too risky to silently re-invoke an agent without operator visibility) but the classification is surfaced in `session-results.json` and `doctor`/`status` so the operator can `dispatch --issues N` to retry with one command. Dispatch is single-threaded by construction (item 28) — the CLI dispatch loop dispatches adapters requests sequentially, never via a thread pool, with a comment citing the documented SQLite-contention ceiling even though this design no longer touches SQLite (the ceiling is presumed to still apply to the devin CLI's own local state, conservatively).
4. **`claude-code`** (NEW, first-class per user's requirement) — implements dossier item 29, promoting the emergent empericus pattern into real code: `worktree.py`'s `create_worktree(repo_root, branch_name, issue_number)` does `git worktree add <sibling-dir>/issue-<N> -b <branch> origin/main` (branched off `origin/main` per the documented job-cannon convention, not local main, so a worker never inherits the orchestrating operator's uncommitted parallel work), the worktree inherits tracked `.claude/settings.json`/hooks automatically (no bespoke copy step needed — this is git's normal behavior), then launches `claude -p <rendered-prompt-file> --cwd <worktree> --dangerously-skip-permissions`-equivalent (exact flag TBD against current Claude Code CLI at build time — flagged as an open verification item, not a design gap) as a subprocess via `subprocess_runner.py`. A `reconcile()` pass (dossier item 29's second half) runs as part of `doctor`/`status`: for every PR whose `mergedBy` isn't the orchestrator's configured bot identity AND whose linked issue is still labeled `agent:in-progress`/`agent:pr-open`/`agent:reviewing`, flag a `DoctorCheck(severity="warning")` "PR #N merged outside merge-ready, issue #M's labels are stale" — this is detection only in v1 (no auto-correction of labels without operator confirmation, matching the "pause on ambiguity" instruction).

**Lifecycle contract (all adapters)**: `dispatch()` → `SessionDispatchResult` (existing dataclass, unchanged shape) → `workflow.py` labels `agent:in-progress` only on `ok=True` AND (for manual) only after confirmation. Error contract: adapters never raise past their own `dispatch()` method — every failure mode (timeout, missing binary, bad encoding, worktree-create failure) is caught and returned as `ok=False, error=<str>`, mirroring `cross_family.py`'s existing never-raises hard contract (explicitly extended to all adapters, not just cross-family, closing a consistency gap the dossier didn't flag but which principle #5/#6 demands — one error-handling shape, not four different ones).

design.state_and_atomicity:
**Schema**: state.json schema v1 is UNCHANGED at the top level (`version`, `generated_at`, `issues{}`, `prs{}`, `events[]`) — this is the hard compatibility constraint for job-cannon's live 38.7KB/55-issue/7-PR/40-event file. `load_state()` already tolerates missing/extra keys via `setdefault` (verified in scaffold) and event-payload schema drift is inherently tolerated since events are read-only history, never re-parsed into typed objects. No version bump needed for anything in this design — every change below is additive-field-only within existing dict shapes (e.g., `state["prs"][n]["rework_cycle_count"]` is a new key, not a renamed one; a state.json missing it just gets it initialized to 0 on first touch via `.get(..., 0)`, exactly the pattern `load_state` already uses for top-level keys).

**Migration safety for job-cannon's in-flight state**: the extraction repo's `state.py` module is copied byte-for-byte compatible (already is — confirmed both forks are byte-identical here and the scaffold matches). The path from job-cannon's current `automation.devin_orchestrator` invocation to the new `devin_orchestrator` package changes only the *import path*, never the *state file location or shape* — `.var/devin-orchestrator/state.json` stays exactly where it is, at the same relative path, written by the same atomic temp-file+`os.replace` routine. Zero migration script needed for state; it just keeps being read/written by the new package once the editable dep swap happens. Verification step before cutover: `devin-orch status --json` against job-cannon's live `.var/devin-orchestrator/` with the new package installed, diffed against the last `automation.devin_orchestrator status --json` output — byte-for-byte data equality required before deleting the old in-repo copy (see migration_plan).

**Fixes applied (item 4, state-clobbering)**: `review()` currently does `state['prs'][str(pr_number)] = {...}` (wholesale replace, confirmed in the scaffold's workflow.py:268 — this bug SURVIVED the union, it is NOT yet fixed). Fix: change to `state['prs'].setdefault(str(pr_number), {}).update({...})`, matching the pattern `record_review()` and `merge_ready()` already correctly use (`.setdefault(...).update(...)`, confirmed present at workflow.py:339 and :395). `intake()` has the same wholesale-replace bug at workflow.py:109 (`state["issues"][str(issue_number)] = {...}`) — same fix, `.setdefault(...).update(...)`. This is a **one-line-per-call-site fix**, not a redesign, because the merge-update pattern is already the established convention elsewhere in the same file — enforcing it uniformly is exactly "fix at the right abstraction layer" (the layer is "how workflow.py touches state dicts," and three of five call sites already do it right).

**Corrupt-state handling (item 5)**: `load_state()` wraps `json.load()` in try/except `json.JSONDecodeError`, and on failure: renames the corrupt file to `state.json.corrupt-<timestamp>` (never deletes — preserves forensic evidence) and returns `empty_state()`, logging a warning to stderr. No locking is added — this remains a documented single-writer-discipline risk (the CLI is explicitly single-user/single-operator per the repo's own framing; a lock file would be defensive-programming theater for a tool nobody else invokes concurrently, and principle #6 disfavors scattered defensive checks that don't address a real observed failure mode — no concurrent-invocation corruption has been observed in either fork's production history, only the corrupt-JSON gap has). This is called out explicitly in ARCHITECTURE.md as an accepted risk, not silently absent.

**`rework_cycle_count` enforcement (item 13)**: `record_review(decision="request_changes")` increments `state["prs"][pr_number]["rework_cycle_count"]` (new field, defaults 0). When the post-increment count exceeds `config.review.max_rework_cycles`, the decision is force-escalated to `blocked` instead of `request_changes` (labels `agent:human-needed` applied, no rework prompt generated) — implemented as a guard clause at the top of the existing `request_changes` branch, not a new code path, keeping the single-enforcement-point property.

**`required_changes` schema fix (item 15)**: `record_review()`'s decision payload gains `"required_changes": []` (currently omitted, matching `review()`'s template which already includes it) — additive field, and a non-empty-summary validation (`CommandResult(False, "summary must be non-empty for record-review", {})`) added before the write, short-circuiting the pr-650/pr-651 empty-approval pattern at the CLI layer directly (belt-and-suspenders with the janitor pass, which catches it pre-review; this catches it at decision-recording time too, since a human operator typing `record-review` bypasses the janitor entirely).

design.migration_plan:
**Principle**: reversible, additive, zero-downtime for job-cannon's 55 in-flight issues / 7 open PRs. Both consumer repos keep their `.var/devin-orchestrator/` and `orchestrator.config.yaml` (or equivalent) exactly where they are — repo-local state and config never move.

**Step 1 — package readiness (devin-orchestrator repo, no consumer impact)**: land every fix in `fixes_included` here first, run the full test suite, tag `v0.1.0`. This is pure repo-local work with zero blast radius on job-cannon/empericus.

**Step 2 — job-cannon migration (higher risk, 55 issues/7 PRs live)**:
1. `git rev-parse HEAD` snapshot both job-cannon and devin-orchestrator (pre_fix_hash pattern per user's memory) before touching anything.
2. Add `[tool.uv.sources] devin-orchestrator = { path = "../devin-orchestrator", editable = true }` and `devin-orchestrator` to `[project.dependencies]` in job-cannon's `pyproject.toml`. `uv sync`.
3. Update every job-cannon call site (CLI aliases, any wrapper scripts, CI workflow files if any reference `python -m automation.devin_orchestrator`) to `python -m devin_orchestrator` / the installed `devin-orch` console script — grep confirmed no wrapper script currently exists outside tests/docs, so this is likely a small, enumerable set of edits (docs/devin-orchestration/*.md references, any shell alias in the operator's own dotfiles — out of repo scope, flag to user).
4. Copy job-cannon's `orchestrator.config.yaml`-equivalent (currently `automation/devin_orchestrator/orchestrator.config.yaml`, INSIDE the package per the dossier's item 21 finding — this itself needs to move to job-cannon's repo root as part of migration, since it's per-repo deployment data) to `<job-cannon-root>/orchestrator.config.yaml`. Diff every field against `examples/orchestrator.config.devin.yaml` to confirm no silent default drift (e.g., verify `required_checks` list, `delete_branch: true`, `cross_family.enabled: true` all carry over explicitly since the new package's dataclass defaults differ in `delete_branch` per this design's P1-11 fix).
5. **Do NOT touch `.var/devin-orchestrator/state.json` or any artifact under it.** Verify byte-identical `RuntimePaths` resolution: `runtime.state_dir` default `.var/devin-orchestrator` is unchanged, so the new package resolves to the exact same directory job-cannon already has 55 issues/7 PRs/40 events in.
6. Verification gate before deleting old code: run `devin-orch status --json` (new package) and diff against the last known-good output of the old `python -m automation.devin_orchestrator status --json` — must match on `ready_issue_count`, `available_issue_count`, `active_issue_count`, `open_linked_pr_count`, and every issue/PR number present. Also run `devin-orch doctor` fresh and confirm no new blocking findings versus the old required_checks/labels reality.
7. Only after step 6 passes: delete `automation/devin_orchestrator/` from job-cannon (git rm, single commit, reversible via git history — never a destructive op per the Git Safety Protocol) and delete the now-redundant `tests/test_devin_orchestrator.py` from job-cannon (coverage now lives in the extracted repo).
8. **In-flight session compatibility**: none of the 7 open PRs or 55 issues have any in-progress *code-level* dependency on the old package's import path — all durable references are GitHub labels + on-disk JSON/markdown artifacts (per the dossier's own §3 finding that GitHub + `.var` artifacts, not Python object identity, are the real state). This means the migration is safe to perform mid-cycle: an issue dispatched under the old code and a PR reviewed under the new code interoperate freely because they only ever communicated through `state.json` + GitHub, both of which are schema-stable across this migration.

**Step 3 — empericus migration (lower risk, zero live `.var` state)**:
Same steps 2.1-2.4, 2.7 (no state to migrate/verify at step 2.5-2.6 since empericus has no `.var/devin-orchestrator/` on disk at all — confirmed empty). Empericus's `orchestrator.config.yaml`-equivalent already correctly ships `delete_branch: false` with the documented worktree rationale — this carries over as-is and now matches the new package's corrected default (P1-11), so this consumer needs zero config-value changes, only the path-dependency + import-path swap.

**Rollback**: at any point before step 2.7/3's deletion commit, reverting is `git checkout -- pyproject.toml uv.lock orchestrator.config.yaml` plus removing the added `[tool.uv.sources]` block — the old `automation/devin_orchestrator/` package is untouched until the explicit deletion commit, so rollback before that point is a no-op revert, not a data-recovery exercise.
risks: The scaffold's dossier-stated status ('41 tests, DONE: merge/label decoupling, config discovery, prompt-dir overrides, worker_template selection') undersells actual progress — doctor.py, cross_family.py, spec-review, and --issues dispatch are ALL already implemented and passing (50 tests). This design's fix list above was cross-checked against the live code, not the dossier's status note, to avoid re-litigating already-solved problems; still, the state-clobbering bug (P0-4) is a real regression risk since it's easy to assume 'union merge = all P0s closed' when in fact 2 of 8 P0s (state-clobbering, and the --issues space-mangling emp bug) survived the union unfixed.

job-cannon's live state.json holds 55 issues / 7 PRs / 40 events (not the dossier's stated 'four issues in flight') — the migration plan's verification gate (byte-for-byte status diff before deleting old code) is treated as non-negotiable given this larger real blast radius; skipping step 2.6 to save time is the single highest-risk shortcut available and should not be taken.

devin-shell adapter's session-tracking design deliberately sidesteps open question 2 (does --print persist to sessions.db) by using a self-owned sidecar JSON + exit-code + --export tracking instead of SQLite polling — this is a design choice, not a resolution of the open question; if a future need arises to correlate with Devin's own session store (e.g. for `devin --resume`), the sidecar-only approach won't have that linkage. Accepted trade-off: avoids the documented single-threaded SQLite-contention ceiling and the undocumented-schema fragility entirely, at the cost of not being able to resume a devin-shell-launched session via the Devin CLI's own resume mechanism.

Removing the command adapter's shell=True string-form (P0-2) is a breaking config-schema change for any hypothetical consumer using that form — confirmed unused in both current production configs, but this is a point-in-time fact, not a structural guarantee; if a third consumer of this package appears before this design ships, re-verify.

confirm-dispatch (new CLI command, companion to the manual-adapter honesty fix) adds one more manual step to the manual-adapter workflow, which is the fallback path both forks' production dispatch mostly bypasses anyway (per dossier §7 dedup note, item 3 and item 29 are 'two faces of the same root issue') — if devin-shell/claude-code adapters are adopted quickly, this added friction on the deprecated-in-practice manual path is low-cost; if an operator keeps using manual adapter as primary, this is a net new step they must remember, flagged as a UX trade-off accepted in exchange for closing the fabricated-success bug.

Bright idea Q (hook-veto-chain refactor of merge_ready's monolithic gate) and P (structured-disagreement review protocol) were explicitly NOT folded into this design — Q is a clean refactor target noted as 'not urgent, worth doing alongside item A' by the dossier itself, and implementing it now would touch merge_ready's already-correct P0/P1-fixed logic for stylistic reasons only, adding change-surface to a function this design otherwise leaves alone; P changes the semantics of the existing validated 'independent veto, not consensus' cross-family design (item C, HIGH-verdict, already correct) in a way the dossier itself says needs explicit design-panel sign-off before implementing — rejected for this pass, revisit only if cross-family review's current framing proves insufficient in practice.

Bright ideas I (doom-loop detection via transcript polling), J (route/retry across worker architecture), K (diversity-favoring parallel-dispatch selection), L (per-worker cost/token circuit breaker), N (three-tier context), O (risk-scored review-depth routing), R (status-grid dashboard), S/T/U (branch-protection self-approval quirk, kanban-card correspondence, manager-of-managers) — all explicitly REJECTED for this build per the dossier's own MEDIUM/LOW verdicts: I is recorded as a natural follow-on once --export capture ships (this design ships the capture point but not the polling logic — deliberately staged, not omitted by oversight); J/K need dispatch-history data this system doesn't have yet; L/N/O/R are UX or cost-optimization enhancements with no correctness stake; S/T/U's underlying invariants (separate-actor review, worktree/state correspondence, trajectory-mining) are partially covered already by this design's `reconcile` command and adapter error-contract, making the GUI/platform-specific originals moot.

The janitor pass (new, bright idea A/E) and the max_rework_cycles enforcement (P1-13) both change observable behavior for existing in-flight PRs the moment the migrated package is live — a PR currently sitting in `agent:reviewing` with an empty review-decision.json will, on the next `review()` pass, get a fresh janitor evaluation it never had before. This is intended (it's the whole point of the fix) but means job-cannon's 7 open PRs should be spot-checked post-migration for any janitor findings that weren't visible under the old code, rather than assuming silent continuity.

No file-locking was added to state.json (P0-5 fix is corrupt-JSON handling only, not concurrency) — explicitly accepted as a non-fix because no concurrent-invocation corruption has been observed in either fork's production history; if the operator ever runs two `devin-orch loop` invocations concurrently (e.g. via two terminal sessions or an accidental cron overlap), last-writer-wins data loss remains possible. Flagged, not fixed, per principle #6's guidance against defensive checks for unobserved failure modes — revisit if it's ever actually observed.

design.summary: Scaffold already has 8/11 modules solid (config discovery, doctor with dynamic CI-check derivation, decoupled merge/label/branch-delete, atomic state I/O, prompt-dir overrides, worker_template selection). Net-new modules: adapters/worktree.py, adapters/devin_shell.py, adapters/claude_code.py, janitor.py, rework.py (cycle-cap), reconcile.py (stale-label GC per dossier item 29). design.adapter_design:
**Protocol** (`adapters/__init__.py`):
```python
class WorkerAdapter(Protocol):
    name: str
    def dispatch_one(self, repo_root: Path, request: SessionRequest, config: DevinConfig) -> SessionDispatchResult: ...
```
`dispatch_sessions()` keeps its existing shape (write manifest, loop adapters, write results) but resolves the adapter via a plain `dict[str, WorkerAdapter]` literal built in `__init__.py` — e.g. `_ADAPTERS = {"manual": ManualAdapter(), "command": CommandAdapter(), "devin-shell": DevinShellAdapter(), "claude-code": ClaudeCodeAdapter()}`. This is explicitly NOT an entry-point/plugin registry (no `importlib.metadata`, no dynamic discovery) — adding a 5th adapter means adding a key to this literal and a module, a one-file diff, matching the no-framework mandate. Unknown adapter name → same clear per-request error as today.

**Lifecycle contract** (same for all 4 adapters, unifying today's inconsistent manual-vs-command semantics):
- `ok=True` means "the orchestrator successfully handed off work" — for `manual` that's now explicitly "manifest written, awaiting confirmation" (not fabricated success); for `command`/`devin-shell`/`claude-code` it means "subprocess launched without immediate error" (0-exit for `command`'s synchronous model; PID alive after a short grace period for the Popen-based ones).
- `ok=True` drives `agent:queued` (new, wired) not `agent:in-progress` directly — see labels.py. `agent:in-progress` is promoted by the `reconcile` pass once independent evidence of real progress exists (a PID still alive, or a branch pushed to origin, or a PR open) rather than trusting the launch call's own success bit. This directly fixes dossier item 3 (fabricated success) without special-casing manual vs. the others — the SAME promotion rule applies uniformly.
- Errors never raise past `dispatch_one()` — always return `ok=False` with `.error` set (matches cross_family.py's proven never-raise contract, extended to adapters per dossier item 7's centralization ask).
- Subprocess execution is centralized in one helper (`adapters/__init__.py::_run_subprocess()` and `_popen_session()`) used by `command.py`, `devin_shell.py`, `claude_code.py` — `encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'` always set, `TimeoutExpired.stdout` bytes-safety always applied. This is the single-point-of-enforcement fix for dossier item 7 rather than four separate copy-pasted subprocess blocks.

**devin-shell specifics**: Popen (non-blocking) not subprocess.run, because a `--print` session can run for minutes and the orchestrator must not block dispatch of the next issue on it. PID + branch_name + start_time recorded to `<state_dir>/dispatches/sessions/issue-<N>.json` (structured sidecar, replacing dossier item 30's grep-based branch recovery). No SQLite dependency at all — sidesteps the unresolved `sessions.db` persistence question (dossier open-Q2) entirely rather than betting the design on it. Single-threaded dispatch (dossier item 28) enforced by dispatching sequentially within one `dispatch_sessions()` call — Popen itself doesn't block, so this only serializes the ~milliseconds of process-spawn overhead, not the worker's actual runtime.

**claude-code specifics**: worktree-first. `dispatch_one()` never launches `claude` unless `launch_headless: true`; default mirrors the dossier's own observed production reality (human pastes the prompt) while making worktree setup itself fully automatic — this closes the literal gap dossier item 29 names ("promote the emergent pattern into real code") without forcing headless automation nobody asked for. Prompt file lands inside the worktree at `.devin-orchestrator/worker-prompt.md` (repo-relative, so `.claude/hooks` running cwd-relative — per dossier §4's confirmed hook behavior — can find it too if a hook ever wants to).

design.state_and_atomicity:
**Schema: UNCHANGED, v1 stays v1.** This is the hard compatibility constraint (job-cannon has 4 issues in flight against the live state.json) and the design deliberately does not touch `STATE_VERSION`, the top-level `issues`/`prs`/`events` keys, or any existing field. All new capability (rework-cycle counting, janitor findings, reconcile results) is derived by reading the existing `events` array at call time — zero new persisted fields required for rework-cap enforcement, since `record_review` already appends a `record_review` event with `{"pr_number": N, "decision": "request_changes"}` on every rework request; `rework_cycle_count(state, pr_number)` is a pure `len([e for e in events if e["kind"]=="record_review" and e["payload"].get("pr_number")==pr_number and e["payload"].get("decision")=="request_changes"])` — no schema migration needed, works retroactively on job-cannon's existing 200-event-capped history.

Two schema-adjacent additions, both additive and optional-read (old state.json readers/writers are unaffected, new code tolerates their absence via `.get(..., default)`):
- `state["prs"][n]["rework_cycles"]` — a denormalized cache of the count above, written by `record_review` for O(1) doctor/status display; NOT the source of truth (the events array is), so if it's ever absent (pre-migration state files) it's recomputed from events on read, never trusted blindly. This directly follows dossier bright-idea M's confirmed principle: local state is a cache/checkpoint, GitHub + the append-only event log are authoritative.
- `state["issues"][n]["queued_at"]` — timestamp for the new `agent:queued` label promotion (labels.py), same additive/optional pattern.

**Atomicity fixes** (dossier items 4, 5 — status: item 4 already appears fixed in the current scaffold via `state["prs"].setdefault(...).update(data)` in `merge_ready` and `record_review`, confirmed by reading workflow.py; `intake()` and `review()` still do wholesale dict-replace on `state["issues"][n]`/`state["prs"][n]` — this is a **regression the scaffold has NOT actually fixed for `review()`/`intake()`**, only for `record_review`/`merge_ready`. Fix: apply the same `.setdefault(...).update()` merge pattern to `intake()` and `review()`'s state writes, closing the gap uniformly rather than leaving two of four write sites still clobbering.

Item 5 (no locking, uncaught JSONDecodeError): `load_state` gets a `try/except json.JSONDecodeError` that backs up the corrupt file to `state.json.corrupt-<timestamp>` and returns `empty_state()` with a logged warning, rather than crashing with a raw traceback — matches the "graceful reset" fix prescribed. File locking: given single-operator/Windows-first framing (per the extraction's own stated scope) and that `os.replace` is already atomic, a full lock manager is over-engineering for this scale — instead, `save_state` gains a **read-verify-write** discipline: it re-reads the file's `generated_at` immediately before replacing and if it changed since this call's `load_state()` read (another process wrote in between), it logs a warning and retries the merge once against the fresh data rather than blindly overwriting. This is optimistic concurrency, not a lock — appropriate for a system with, per the dossier's own admission, at most 1-2 concurrent orchestrator invocations in practice (single operator), and avoids introducing `filelock` as a new dependency.

**Merge/label decoupling** (already done per scaffold status) and the janitor/rework/reconcile additions read `state.json` and GitHub but never become a second source of truth for review decisions — `review-decision.json` on disk remains authoritative for the merge gate (dossier open-Q4 resolved explicitly: **keep local-file-as-authority, status quo**, because moving to a PR-comment or GitHub-native review adds a new failure mode — parsing structured data back out of free-text comments — for no correctness gain over the current atomic-write JSON file; the fix is enforcing the read-fresh-never-cache discipline `_review_decision()` already implements, not relocating the data).

**New subcommands:**

- `confirm-dispatch --issue N` — the manual-adapter promotion path: flips `agent:queued` → `agent:in-progress` for an issue whose manual dispatch manifest entry the operator has now actually acted on (opened a real Devin/Claude session). This is the concrete mechanism that makes dossier item 3's fix (manual ok=True ≠ real launch) operable rather than just "stuck at queued forever" — closes the loop the fabricated-success bug left open.

**doctor additions** (2 new checks alongside the existing 8):

design.migration_plan:
**Zero data migration** — this is a pure dependency-and-import relocation, not a state transformation, because STATE_VERSION stays 1 and `.var/devin-orchestrator/`'s directory layout is unchanged.

Per consumer repo (job-cannon first, since it has 4 issues in flight and is the higher-risk migration; empericus second):

1. **Add the editable path dependency** in the consumer's `pyproject.toml`:
   ```toml
   [tool.uv.sources]
   devin-orchestrator = { path = "../devin-orchestrator", editable = true }
   ```
   and `devin-orchestrator` under `[project.dependencies]` (or a `dev`/`automation` extra if the consumer wants it non-default). `uv sync` picks it up as an editable install — `devin-orch` becomes available on the consumer's own venv without a publish step, matching the repo's `[project.scripts]` entry point already defined.

2. **Delete the vendored copy**: `git rm -r automation/devin_orchestrator/` (job-cannon) / `automation/devin_orchestrator/` (empericus) — both are already git-excluded per the dossier (`.git/info/exclude` for job-cannon, tracked `.gitignore` for empericus), so this is a working-tree deletion, not a history-rewriting operation. Any host-repo-tracked file that referenced the old in-package location (docs, CI workflow steps invoking `python -m automation.devin_orchestrator` or similar) gets a mechanical import-path update to `devin-orch <subcommand>` (the console script) or `python -m devin_orchestrator` (module invocation both still work since `__main__.py` is unchanged).

3. **`.var/devin-orchestrator/` state is left exactly where it is** — `runtime.state_dir` still defaults to `.var/devin-orchestrator` relative to repo root, and `find_repo_root`/`runtime_paths` resolution is unchanged, so the existing 4-in-flight-issue state.json, issue prompt dirs, PR review packets, and decision files are read by the new package with zero changes. This is the single most important invariant for job-cannon: **do not touch `.var/` during migration**, verify with `devin-orch status` immediately after cutover that the same active-issue/PR counts are reported as before the swap.

4. **`orchestrator.config.yaml` at each consumer's repo root is left in place, unmodified** — `find_config_path` already resolves it there (dossier item 21 confirmed done), so no config file move is needed. The only optional step is adopting the new `devin.worktree_root`/`launch_headless`/`export_transcript` fields if the consumer wants the new adapters; both consumers can keep `adapter: manual` indefinitely with zero behavior change beyond the fabricated-success fix (P0-3) — which is a **behavior change worth flagging to the operator**: manual dispatch now applies `agent:queued` instead of `agent:in-progress` until `confirm-dispatch` is run. For job-cannon's 4 in-flight issues, this only affects *future* dispatches, not the currently-active ones (their labels are already `agent:in-progress` on GitHub and nothing in this migration touches existing GitHub label state).

5. **Design-doc corpus migration** (job-cannon's unversioned `.var/devin-orchestrator/*.md` — 10 files, one `git clean` from permanent loss): copy the reconciled/trimmed versions into `devin-orchestrator/docs/ops-notes/` (this repo) as the versioned home, since the reasoning applies to the shared package, not to job-cannon specifically. The original files in job-cannon's `.var/` are left in place untouched (they're just data at that point, not load-bearing) — no deletion, no risk to in-flight state.

6. **Verification gate before calling either migration done**: run `devin-orch doctor` and `devin-orch status --json` in both consumer repos post-cutover, diff the `status --json` issue/PR counts against a pre-migration snapshot taken with the old vendored copy, confirm they match exactly. Then run each repo's own test suite (job-cannon's / empericus's, not devin-orchestrator's own 41+ tests) to confirm nothing else imported `automation.devin_orchestrator` directly (dossier's own fragile-seam note: string-target monkeypatches and `tests/__init__.py` sys.path tricks were the old test suites' fragile seam — the new package's tests live entirely in this repo now, so consumer repos should have ZERO of their own devin_orchestrator-specific tests left to break, only integration-level checks like the above).
risks: Windows NTFS-junction detection for worktree.py is the highest-uncertainty implementation detail: os.path.islink() does not reliably detect junctions on Windows (they're reparse points, not symlinks in the POSIX sense); the design commits to shelling out to `fsutil reparsepoint query` or `(Get-Item $path).LinkType` via PowerShell rather than a Python stdlib check, which reintroduces a Windows-only code path — acceptable given the repo is explicitly Windows-first, but must be tested against a real junction fixture (not mocked) before trusting it in production, since a wrong branch here reproduces exactly the shared-venv-destruction hazard this fix exists to prevent.

The devin-shell adapter's entire liveness/tracking design deliberately avoids the sessions.db question (dossier open-Q2) rather than resolving it — this is the right call given the load-bearing premise is contested in the source material, but it means devin-shell sessions are tracked ONLY via PID+sidecar+stdout-log, so a session that survives a Devin CLI *update* changing its process model, or one that daemonizes/detaches from the parent PID, would silently break liveness tracking with no fallback. Mitigate by having `status`/`reconcile` treat 'PID not found' as 'unknown, check GitHub for a PR' rather than 'dead' — never treat process-liveness as authoritative, only as a hint, consistent with the GitHub-is-authoritative principle.

Choosing max_rework_cycles=2 (not the dead-config value of 3, not the research-cited production value of 1) is a judgment call resolving dossier open-Q12 without the user's direct sign-off — flagged here explicitly for confirmation rather than silently picked; rationale: 1 is aggressive for a system just gaining enforcement for the first time (operators used to unlimited cycles need a softer landing), 3 is what the dead config already said and the cited research argues against indefinite-feeling caps, so 2 splits the difference. This is the one open design question in this document I did not treat as settled — recommend confirming with the user before implementation.

P3-32/33/34 (fleet-readiness domain-specific gates, destructive-command matching, gate-layer CI) are scoped OUT of devin-orchestrator itself and pushed to docs/ops-notes/ as guidance for consumer repos to implement in their own .devin/ or .claude/ hook layers. This directly answers dossier open-Q5 (is .devin/ hooks+skills infra in scope) with 'no, it stays host-repo-specific' — correct per SIMPLICITY-FIRST and the observed fact that empericus runs fine without it, but it does mean job-cannon's require_live_scan.py-style re-execution gates get ZERO code-sharing benefit from this extraction; if a third consumer repo wants the same gate pattern, it re-implements it from the ops-notes doc, not from a shared library function. Accepted trade-off, not a silent gap.

janitor.py's ok=False short-circuit behavior resolves dossier open-Q13 (does janitor-fail skip packet generation or annotate it) in favor of the CHEAPER option: skip review-prompt.md generation entirely and route straight to a rework-equivalent state. This trades transparency (the human/reviewer never sees a packet for a janitor-failed PR, only a terse status message) for cost — reconsider if operational experience shows operators want visibility into *why* a packet wasn't generated beyond the janitor's structured finding list already surfaced in `review`'s CommandResult.data.

Explicitly REJECTED bright-ideas from dossier §10, with reasons: (I) doom-loop/transcript-polling detection — rejected as a day-one feature since it depends on --export/transcript harvesting actually working in practice first, which itself is unvalidated (open-Q2); revisit only after devin-shell has real operational hours. (J) route/retry across worker architecture on failure — rejected as premature; no dispatch-history data exists yet to know Devin-vs-Claude-Code failure fingerprints in THIS system, and building routing logic on a guess violates the no-speculative-surface mandate. (K) diversity-favoring parallel-dispatch selection — rejected outright, not applicable; this system has no parallel-dispatch-same-issue feature and none is being added. (L) per-worker cost/token circuit breaker — rejected for this pass; single-operator systems paying per-ACU care about this eventually but it needs the liveness-tracking foundation (devin_shell.py's PID sidecar) to exist and prove itself first; premature to add a cost-anomaly detector against a data source that doesn't exist yet. (N) three-tier context/null-retrieval-as-signal — rejected; the current 'embed full issue body' prompt pattern is adequate at this system's scale, and building a context-retrieval layer is scope creep the dossier itself calls 'not urgent.' (O) risk-scored per-PR cross-family routing — rejected; needs a risk-signal definition that doesn't exist, correctly flagged by the dossier as 'not yet a concrete fix-list item.' (P) structured-disagreement review protocol — rejected; changes cross_family.py's semantics from independent-veto to argumentative-adversarial, which the dossier itself says needs explicit design-panel sign-off before implementing; not assumed here. (Q) hook-veto-chain refactor of merge_ready — partially adopted in spirit (janitor.py IS an independent veto stage ahead of merge_ready) but the dossier's fuller vision of decomposing merge_ready into N independently-vetoing hooks is deferred; today's single-function merge gate with the janitor pass ahead of it is simpler and sufficient at this scale. (R) status-grid dashboard — rejected; `status --json` is adequate for a handful of concurrent workers, a TUI dashboard is UI-philosophy scope creep for a backend-focused single operator per the user's own stated profile. (S) firewall/self-approval branch-protection parity — rejected, doesn't transfer to a single-operator repo where the operator IS the approver by design, exactly as the dossier concludes. (T) kanban-card=worktree periodic-GC pattern — PARTIALLY adopted (reconcile.py's orphaned-worktree detection IS this pattern) but explicitly report-only, never auto-deleting, rejecting the GUI-tooling framing entirely. (U) manager-of-managers / persisted-trajectory-mining — rejected as speculative and dependent on shipped features (transcript export) that don't exist yet; revisit only as a genuinely later milestone.

linked_issue_number's bare #N-in-title over-matching (dossier item 14) is NOT included in the fixes-included list for this design pass — it was flagged in the dossier as still-open but wasn't re-verified against the current scaffold during this design session; recommend a follow-up check before considering P1 complete, since a mis-bound PR silently drives wrong review packets and merge actions.

The read-verify-write optimistic-concurrency mechanism proposed for state.py (in lieu of a real file lock) has not been prototyped; if two orchestrator invocations genuinely race in practice (e.g. a human running `status` while a scheduled `loop` is mid-write), the single-retry-then-warn behavior could still lose an update on a second collision. Given the stated single-operator scale this is judged acceptable, but it is a real gap versus a proper lock file, traded deliberately for zero new dependencies and simplicity.

Remaining work: two adapters (devin-shell, claude-code), a fleet-readiness/janitor gate layer, state-machine hardening (locking, merge-not-clobber, label transition ownership, rework-cycle cap), a `doctor` command expansion, dispatch-wave/--issues fixes plumbed through `loop`, cross-family/spec-review reuse-poisoning fix, prompt hardening (escaping + structured template), a versioned docs suite + ops-notes home for the orphaned design corpus, and the editable-path-dependency migration for job-cannon/empericus preserving their existing 38KB/0KB state.json and repo-local config+prompts. design.adapter_design:
Protocol (in adapters/__init__.py), replacing the current ad hoc if/elif in dispatch_sessions:

class WorkerAdapter(Protocol):
    name: str
    def dispatch(self, request: SessionRequest, config: OrchestratorConfig, repo_root: Path) -> SessionDispatchResult: ...
    def reconcile(self, repo_root: Path, paths: RuntimePaths, gh: GitHub) -> list[ReconciliationFinding]: ...

dispatch_sessions() becomes a thin loop over ADAPTER_REGISTRY[config.devin.adapter] — new adapters register themselves by import, no hardcoded elif chain (satisfies the no-hardcoded-lists rule; an unregistered name still produces the existing clear per-request failure).

Four adapters ship, ranked by contract clarity:

1. manual (fallback, always available). FIX for item 3: the manifest write still succeeds, but dispatch() in workflow.py no longer labels agent:in-progress off the manual adapter's ok flag alone. Manual dispatch produces a result with ok=True, awaiting_confirmation=True, and a new devin-orch confirm-dispatch --issue N command (thin CLI wrapper around the existing label-transition function) is what actually applies agent:in-progress, run by the operator once a session is genuinely open. This is the operator-UX-first answer to the fabricated-success bug: it doesn't add friction to the common case (devin-shell/claude-code adapters still auto-confirm), it just stops manual from lying.

2. command (generic subprocess, kept for bring-your-own launchers). FIX for item 2: string-form shell=True interpolation is removed entirely — only list-form commands are accepted; issue_title is never shell-interpolated. Uses subprocess_runner.py for consistent encoding.

3. devin-shell (new, DEFAULT-documented). Launches devin --prompt-file <FILE> --print --permission-mode dangerous --model <configured> via subprocess_runner.py, cwd = a worktree created by worktree.py (default) or the bare repo root (legacy mode, config-gated). Session attribution via session_tracking.py: snapshot sessions.db (read-only) immediately pre-launch, accept only sessions with created_at >= dispatch_time and id not in snapshot — closes item 24's race. Primary discovery path is devin list --format json (documented) with the SQLite snapshot as fallback only, gated behind an ADR-0002-recorded premise check (doctor verifies this empirically on doctor --adapter-probe rather than assuming). Output capture via worker_output.py: --export <path> alongside stdout redirect, post-exit transcript harvest, structured JSON header/footer (exit code, start/end timestamps). Classifies the 39-byte "Error: A tool was rejected by the user" signature and, on detection, diffs the worktree for salvageable progress and offers (config-gated: auto or operator-confirm) a relaunch with a finish-style prompt. Liveness/timeout supervision: PID + start time tracked in dispatches/session-manifest.json; a max-duration kill+salvage-relaunch path. Dispatch is serialized (a dispatch-lock file) per the documented single-threaded SQLite-contention ceiling — enforced, not just documented.

4. claude-code (new, first-class). Promotes the emergent empericus pattern into real code: worktree.py creates git worktree add <sibling-dir>/issue-<N> -b agent/issue-<N>-<slug> origin/main (off origin/main, matching production practice), junctions/symlinks the shared .venv in with the safe-teardown ordering ported from finish_worker.sh (delete reparse point first via Windows-specific junction deletion; non-Windows: plain symlink is already safe to unlink — the hazard is Windows-only). The .claude/ directory is inherited automatically by ordinary git worktree add checkout — no code needed for that part, it's correctness-by-construction. Launch: claude -p <rendered-prompt-file-contents> --cwd <worktree>, headless. Because "PR merges are done by the human account directly" is the observed empericus reality (a legitimate operating mode, not a bug), claude-code's reconcile() method scans open-linked-PRs-per-issue, detects mergedBy != automation identity on an already-merged PR whose issue is still labeled active, and corrects the stale label to agent:done — wired into status (surfaced as a warning) and offered as devin-orch reconcile (explicit, since silently relabeling on a human's behalf without being asked crosses the "ask, don't assume" line).

Adapter selection: devin.adapter config key unchanged in shape; values become manual | command | devin-shell | claude-code. worker_template (existing, DONE) already correctly pairs with adapter choice via the two example config files.

Lifecycle contract (all adapters): dispatch_sessions() still always writes session-manifest.json first, then always writes session-results.json — unchanged, sound pattern. reconcile() is new on the Protocol but optional (default no-op for manual/command).

Error contract: every adapter method returns SessionDispatchResult/CommandResult-shaped values, never raises for expected failure modes (timeout, missing binary, non-zero exit) — matches cross_family.py's already-correct never-raises discipline, backported via subprocess_runner.py owning all try/except around subprocess.run.

- ReviewConfig's three dead fields (max_rework_cycles, require_tests_or_rationale, require_issue_link) get wired to real enforcement in workflow.py rather than deleted — deleting would break existing YAMLs per the "never remove existing fields" rule; instead they become live.

Prompt resolution (unchanged mechanism, verified DONE): resolve_template(name, search_dirs) — repo-local runtime.prompts_dir searched first, package prompts/ dir as fallback.

FIXES to prompts.py:
- Escaping (item 18): before safe_substitute, injected string values (issue title/body, PR diff excerpts) pass through a fence-safe transform — wrap in a randomized-length code fence so attacker-controlled content containing a matching fence can't escape it.
- Structured template shape (bright-idea G, item 19): worker.md and worker_claude_code.md decomposed into shared partials under prompts/worker_sections/ (Overview, Requirements, Procedure, Specifications, Advice, Forbidden Actions, Required-from-User — the Devin Playbook shape) assembled at render time. This is the concrete fix for rework.md's orphaned /preflight reference: Devin-skills-specific procedure text lives only in worker.md's procedure partial, never inline in rework.md, so a raw-shell (claude-code) deployment physically cannot inherit a skill reference that doesn't apply to it. Per-repo invariants (empericus's privacy/asyncio/migration warnings) inject via a runtime.prompts_dir override of just the relevant partial file, not a full-template fork.
- Every rendered worker.md/worker_claude_code.md includes a self-verification command in its Specifications section, sourced from a new config field dispatch.verification_command (default "" falls back to a generic instruction; consumers set it to e.g. "uv run --active pytest -q --tb=short"). The janitor gate independently re-runs this exact command against the worktree post-dispatch rather than trusting the worker's self-report — the generalized instance of REVIEWER_SCOPE_SCANNER.md's enforcement-by-re-execution pattern, now config-driven instead of domain-specific.
- review.md/cross_family_review.md re-scoped per bright-idea B: prompt text instructs "assume CI-required checks and the janitor pass already caught mechanical/test-failure defects; your job is to find undocumented architectural-convention violations and intent mismatches" — a prompt-text change only.

design.state_and_atomicity:
Schema (unchanged on the wire — critical for the 38KB job-cannon state.json to keep loading):
{version, generated_at, issues: {N: {...}}, prs: {N: {...}}, events: [...]}

No field renames, no version bump required — version:1 stays valid. New writes add fields additively only (e.g. a rework_cycle_count derived-and-cached field, always recomputable from events so its absence in old records is harmless).

FIX 1 — merge-update instead of dict-replace (item 4, highest-confidence bug class): state.py gains an immutable helper merge_record(existing, updates) -> {**existing, **updates}. workflow.py's review() and intake() stop doing state['prs'][n] = new_dict / state['issues'][n] = new_dict and instead merge onto the existing record. Pure function, consistent with the immutability-leaning style rule, single-point-of-enforcement rather than scattered per-call-site checks. Decision authority (open question 4) resolved as: disk review-decision.json remains sole authority for merge-gating (already correct — _review_decision() reads fresh from disk), but state.json's prs[N].decision mirror now survives because it's merged, not replaced — closes the pr-497 gap without changing where gating authority lives.

FIX 2 — locking + corrupt-file recovery (item 5): load_state/save_state wrapped with an O_CREAT|O_EXCL sibling .lock file created before read-modify-write, removed in a finally; on FileExistsError, retry with backoff up to a short timeout then fail with a clear CommandResult rather than corrupting data — single-user-daily-driver-safe (protects against the operator running two terminals). load_state catches JSONDecodeError, backs up the corrupt file to state.json.corrupt-<timestamp>, and returns empty_state() with a warning surfaced in the CLI result rather than an uncaught traceback.

FIX 3 — rework-cycle cap enforcement (item 13, bright-idea D): max_rework_cycles default kept at 3 (honors the already-configured YAML value rather than silently changing operator expectations to 1; ADR-0005 records this as revisitable). Enforcement: count record_review(decision=request_changes) events for the PR's issue from the events array (the reliable append-only history) — on the Nth request_changes, record_review auto-escalates: applies agent:blocked+agent:human-needed, refuses further rework-prompt.md regeneration, explains why in the CLI message.

FIX 4 — label transition ownership (item 12): one new pure function compute_label_transition(current_labels, event, config) -> (add_set, remove_set) replaces scattered ad hoc add/remove calls across dispatch/review/record_review/merge_ready. Every label mutation goes through this function, so needs-rework can no longer be stomped by a subsequent review() re-adding reviewing. agent:queued gets wired as the pre-dispatch-lock-acquired state in the serialized devin-shell/claude-code dispatch path rather than removed.

FIX 5 — schema drift tolerance: event-payload readers use .get() with defaults everywhere, never assume a payload key present in the newest events exists in older ones — already the safe pattern _review_decision() uses; applied consistently to any new event-derived computation (the rework-cycle counter is written this way from day one).

Migration compatibility test: test_migration_state_compat.py loads a redacted copy of job-cannon's actual 38KB state.json as a fixture and asserts load_state -> save_state round-trips without data loss and without raising — concrete verification that "4 in-flight issues must keep working" is met, not just assumed.

Atomic writes (unchanged, verified correct): temp-file + os.replace, already Windows-safe. The lock file (FIX 2) wraps the read-modify-write window without changing the atomic final-write step.

design.migration_plan:
Goal: job-cannon and empericus both switch from an untracked, git-excluded in-repo copy (automation/devin_orchestrator/, invoked as python -m automation.devin_orchestrator) to an editable path dependency on the new package, invoked as devin-orch, with zero disruption to job-cannon's 4 in-flight issues.

Step 1 — package the new repo as installable (already true: pyproject.toml has project.scripts devin-orch pointing at devin_orchestrator.cli:main and a proper src/ layout — verified, no work needed).

Step 2 — add the editable path dependency in each consumer:
[tool.uv.sources] devin-orchestrator = { path = "../devin-orchestrator", editable = true }
[project] dependencies += "devin-orchestrator"
Run uv sync in each consumer — uv's editable path-dependency support means local edits to the new repo are picked up without reinstalling.

Step 3 — relocate repo-local config + prompts (state stays put):
- automation/devin_orchestrator/orchestrator.config.yaml moves to the consumer repo root as orchestrator.config.yaml (matches find_config_path's discovery convention). job-cannon keeps delete_branch:true explicit, empericus keeps delete_branch:false explicit — both survive the dataclass default flip untouched because both already set the key.
- Prompts: each consumer's customized worker template moves to a new runtime.prompts_dir (e.g. orchestrator-prompts/ at each repo root, git-tracked), set via the already-shipped prompts_dir config key. Empericus's inlined privacy/asyncio/migration invariants move into a worker_sections/specifications_override.md partial rather than a full worker.md fork.
- .devin/ hooks+skills infra (job-cannon-only) stays host-repo-specific WIP per open question 5's resolution (recorded in ADR-0004) — not shipped as a default scaffold since it's job-cannon-domain-coupled and empericus proves the kit runs without it.

Step 4 — state.json compatibility (the load-bearing constraint):
- No migration script needed. The wire schema is unchanged — job-cannon's existing 38KB state.json (4 issues in flight) is read by the new package's load_state() exactly as before; the merge-update fix only changes how future writes behave. The .var/devin-orchestrator/ directory itself stays exactly where it is — dispatches/, issues/, prs/, logs/, cross-family/ subdirectories untouched.
- Verification before cutover: run devin-orch doctor (new package, --repo pointed at job-cannon) as a dry check, then diff devin-orch status output against the old python -m automation.devin_orchestrator status output. test_migration_state_compat.py (redacted copy of job-cannon's actual file) is the automated version of this same check, run once in the new repo's own CI.
- Cutover order per consumer: (1) add path dependency + uv sync, (2) copy config/prompts to new locations, (3) run doctor + status side-by-side with the old command to confirm parity, (4) switch documented/scripted invocations (setup_worker.sh/finish_worker.sh, batch scripts, docs) from python -m automation.devin_orchestrator to devin-orch, (5) only then delete automation/devin_orchestrator/ (or leave briefly as rollback fallback for one cycle — cheap insurance since it's already git-excluded).
- The untracked .var/devin-orchestrator/ design-doc corpus (job-cannon-only, ~10 files) migrates into the new repo's docs/adr/ as part of Step 1's docs work, independent of the consumer cutover timeline — closes the "one git clean from permanent loss" risk immediately.

Rollback safety: the old automation/devin_orchestrator/ module is left in place (not deleted) until Step 5, so either consumer can revert to the old invocation at any point during migration before parity is confirmed — no destructive step happens early.

Best single-operator daily-loop ergonomics: confirm-dispatch and reconcile are scoped tightly (report-only by default, explicit --fix/--apply), doctor gets meaningful new checks (worktree writability, rework-cycle-near-cap warning), and the worker-prompt partial-template refactor (worker_sections/) structurally prevents the class of drift that caused the /preflight orphan reference rather than patching around one instance of it. rejected_ideas: Any design that treats the manual-adapter 'confirm-dispatch' extra CLI step as low-cost — dossier explicitly states production dispatch in both forks essentially bypasses the manual adapter entirely (setup_worker.sh labels directly, empericus never launches programmatically), so this fix mainly hardens a path nobody uses while adding a step operators must remember on the rare occasions they do use it. risk-first's WorktreeConfig.venv_junction opt-in-defaults-False (falls back to full uv sync per worktree) — reasonable safety default but silently reintroduces the multi-minute-per-dispatch cold-sync cost that the shared-junction pattern existed specifically to avoid; if adopted, doctor must warn loudly when junction mode is off and worktree adapters are in use, or operators will be confused why dispatch got slow.

Reviving devin.adapter dispatch.worker_template mismatch as merely a soft doctor nudge (risk-first) — given this is exactly the kind of drift that caused the rework.md /preflight orphan bug in production, a soft warning is weaker than simplicity/operator-ux-first's structural partial-template fix; prefer the structural fix.

Building max_rework_cycles enforcement around any specific numeric default without flagging it prominently as a judgment call needing explicit operator sign-off — simplicity-first is the only design that flags its own choice (2) as unresolved/needing confirmation; risk-first and operator-ux-first both silently pick 3 (the dead config default) with brief justification. Given principle #8 (pause on ambiguity, don't infer the aggressive interpretation), simplicity-first's explicit flagging is the right posture, but the actual number should be confirmed with the operator before shipping regardless of which design is chosen.

Any full file-locking (mutex/O_EXCL lock file) scheme for state.json — dossier and all three designs agree this is a single-operator local tool with no observed concurrent-corruption incidents; risk-first's explicit non-fix (documented risk) is more honest than operator-ux-first's O_EXCL lock-file addition, which adds real complexity (retry/backoff/stale-lock cleanup) against a failure mode that has never been observed. Simplicity-first's optimistic-concurrency read-verify-write is a reasonable middle ground if something is wanted at all, but plain documentation (risk-first) is sufficient for a 24-hour ship target.
